contradictions.fact: Route grade vs crux pitch grade

claims.says: 5.8, crux=false, notes: 'Pitch 1 climbs Mourning Star (5.8) up to the Zoom anchor before breaking onto this route'
5.7, crux=true (the Flake pitch)

contradictions.internal_resolution: The only 5.8 pitch belongs to a different route (Mourning Star); the crux pitch of Leave My Flake Alone itself is graded 5.7, below the stated overall grade.

Not viable — approach trail and route are largely snow-covered with high avalanche hazard on surrounding slopes during May-June snowmelt.

contradictions.internal_resolution: Likely not a true contradiction — the two claims describe different time-of-year windows — but worth a second look.

contradictions.fact: Direction of travel from La Bohn Gap to the summit

claims.says: rising directly west of La Bohn Gap... standard line follows a climbers' path east/northeast from the gap up the ridge and face above La Bohn Lakes... to the summit
South/southwest basin slopes above upper Necklace Valley, below La Bohn Gap
ascend talus and open slopes on the southwest side, staying left (west/south) of the broad west ridge, to gain La Bohn Peak's summit
Descend the same southwest-slope talus and open ground back down to La Bohn Gap
ascend talus and open slopes on the southwest side, staying left (west/south) of the broad west ridge
staying left — west and south — of the broad west ridge

contradictions.why: The overview says the route climbs 'east/northeast from the gap,' but the peak sits west of the gap (per the overview's own first sentence), and every other field (face, approach, descent_text, climbing_route, approach_variants) says the route goes west/southwest from the gap. The bivy notes confirm 'east... from the gap' is actually the way to neighboring Mount Hinman, not La Bohn Peak.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Six fields (including the overview's own peak-position sentence) agree the route goes west/southwest from the gap; the 'east/northeast' clause in overview is the outlier and appears to be contaminated from the Mount Hinman description.
